name: November 3, 2026 General Election
method: Contests, candidate names, parties and public question text transcribed from the Indiana Voters portal's "Who's On My Ballot" page for precinct Concord 33 (viewed 2026-10-30). Background from web search summaries of the cited pages plus a few pages opened in full (Wikipedia, Concord Community Schools board bios, Indiana courts release); several news sites blocked direct reading (403).
districtHint: The Indiana Voters portal ("Election Districts") lists your precinct and districts.
coverageNote: Covered: Elkhart County precinct Concord 33 (Goshen), including statewide offices, both public questions, judicial retention, U.S. House District 2, State House District 21, county offices, Commissioner District 1, Council District 4, Concord Township and Concord Community Schools District 1. Other precincts' local races aren't covered. Always check your own ballot.

positions.t: Campaigns on shrinking the federal bureaucracy and restoring fiscal responsibility; voted in 2026 against extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits.

about.t: Three commissioners run county government. Each lives in a district but is elected countywide. District 1 covers Concord and Washington townships.

Data centers are a live local issue: the city of Elkhart paused new data center and battery storage applications 9-0 in August, a data center is proposed near Bristol, and residents have asked the county for similar limits. No county-wide rule was found.

positions.t: Incumbent District 1 commissioner; liaison to the St. Joseph River Basin drainage board.
Hasn't held county office; a frequent Democratic candidate for Congress (since 1986) and county council (2012, 2018, 2024).

notes.t: Retired chemist (Whitehall Laboratories, Apex Pharmaceutical) and former science teacher; DePauw chemistry graduate. Lives in Elkhart.

positions.t: Campaign sign promises a balanced budget and fiscal accountability.
Independent candidate (side A of party_governance includes preference for independent leadership).

notes.t: Campaigns against data centers and battery storage sites in the county; her sign also lists 'strong property rights'. Meets voters regularly at a local market.
No campaign website or biography was found.

about.t: The three-member board approves the trustee's budget. Adkins, Beck and Davis won the four-way Republican primary over former board member Kim Mansell; Turner was unopposed for the Democrats.

positions.t: In 2022 praised the board for having 'managed to keep taxes down' and wanted to 'continue in the path that we are on'.

notes.t: Retired after 38 years with the Concord Township Fire Department. Also ran in 2022.
Also ran for this board in 2022.
Truck driver; retired in 2021 after 16 years as a Concord Township firefighter-paramedic. In 2022 wanted help for seniors and veterans facing ambulance bills and more fire and ambulance equipment.

flags.t: Adkins's and Davis's views are from 2022. Nothing was found on Beck's or Turner's views.

contests.instructions: Check your ballot for how many to pick; this may be two or three seats.

about.t: Concord board members must live in a district, but everyone in the school district votes on every seat. In 2022 the ballot allowed up to three picks, at most one from District 2, which means two District 1 seats.

In 2022 three seats were open and these same three ran in District 1. Concord's site now lists all three as board members, so this may be three seats for three candidates; the county list doesn't say.

positions.t: On the board since 2015; now board president.

notes.t: Corporate treasurer at Indiana Wood Products; former PTO president at South Side Elementary.

At a 2022 League of Women Voters forum: the board must provide the best staff, programs and facilities 'in a fiscally responsible way', and the failed school referendum showed taxpayers' views on spending. Sees the board as 'partners with our administration'.

positions.t: Concord's site lists him as a board member first elected in 2022.

notes.t: Training coordinator for Elkhart County Court Services (juvenile detention and probation); 15+ years in law enforcement and corrections; church deacon and youth volunteer.

At the 2022 forum he welcomed closer public scrutiny of school boards, citing parents' pushback on critical race theory in Virginia ('and rightfully so'), and noted that voters who defeated the referendum asked the board to stop 'wasteful spending'. Urged residents to attend board meetings.

positions.t: Appointed in 2022, then elected; now board secretary.

notes.t: Bookkeeper; former South Side Elementary PTO president and substitute in Concord schools.

At the 2022 forum: students should be 'challenged' and leave with problem-solving and teamwork skills, 'not just academic masters'; wants teachers to have the resources they need and is 'proud to be a part of the team' in place.
School board races are nonpartisan; none of these candidates declared a party.

flags.t: Candidate views are from 2022, and the number of seats isn't confirmed.
